2609.20143.title: Designing Against Deskilling: Metacognitive Feedback Reduces Cognitive Offloading to LLM Assistants
2609.20143.paper_summary: Cognitive offloading to AI can reduce opportunities to practice skills, creating risks of deskilling. However, it remains unclear how to prevent deskilling without restricting access to AI. Here, we design two interventions to reduce offloading decisions: (1) metacognitive feedback that makes the implications of offloading for users explicit, and (2) an effort-based reward that incentivizes less extensive LLM assistance. We test both in a preregistered online experiment ($N = 704$) with a 2$\times$2 design and a no-AI control. The task was to practice fraction arithmetic with an LLM-based assistant that provided solutions only on explicit request, followed by an unaided test. Metacognitive feedback reduced answer offloading (OR $= 0.47$) and improved test performance (OR $= 1.51$). We found no evidence that the reward affected either outcome. Our results identify metacognitive feedback as a promising design choice to reduce cognitive offloading.
2609.20143.paper_summary_zh: 認知外部化到人工智慧可能減少練習技能的機會，並造成技能退化的風險。<lb/>然而，如何在不限制對人工智慧的訪問情況下防止技能退化仍然不清楚。<lb/>在此，我們設計了兩項干預措施以減少外部化決策：<lb/>(1) 使外部化對用戶的影響明確的元認知反饋，<lb/>以及 (2) 一種基於努力的獎勵，激勵較少依賴大型語言模型的協助。<lb/>我們在一項預註冊的線上實驗中測試了這兩者（$N = 704$），採用2$\times$2設計和無人工智慧控制組。<lb/>任務是與一個基於大型語言模型的助手練習分數算術，該助手僅在明確要求下提供解決方案，然後進行無幫助的測試。<lb/>元認知反饋減少了答案的外部化（OR $= 0.47$）並改善了測試表現（OR $= 1.51$）。<lb/>我們未發現獎勵對任何結果有影響的證據。<lb/>我們的結果確定元認知反饋是一個有前景的設計選擇，以減少認知外部化。
